text_blocks.snippet: Recent reports from law enforcement and federal prosecutors highlight several active scams targeting residents across Central Illinois:
snippet_highlighted_words: several active scams targeting residents across Central Illinois

list.snippet: Federal Prosecutor & Law Enforcement Impersonation: Scammers spoof phone numbers and use real names of staff from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois or local sheriffs' offices, demanding money or financial details over the phone (such as fake threats or phony pre-trial release/GPS monitoring fees) .

AI Voice-Cloning & Romance Scams: Criminals use artificial intelligence and voice-mimicking tools to simulate family members in distress or build long-term online connections to swindle victims out of thousands of dollars.

Fake Rental & Real Estate Listings: Scammers steal real online property photos and list them at "too good to be true" prices in areas like Galesburg, claiming the owner is out of town and demanding wire transfers or gift cards.
Driveway Paving & Home Repair Fraud: Itinerant contractors offer shoddy, overpriced, or unfinished paving and construction services while demanding upfront cash payment.
Social Media & Online Shopping Scams: Fake store pages and discounted trending products on platforms like Facebook and Instagram take money without delivering goods (or send counterfeit items).
Phishing & Text Scams: Phishing texts and emails (including fake utility, DMV, or explicit-photo extortion threats demanding Bitcoin) use publicly scraped personal data to create false urgency.
Verify the caller: Hang up and call back using a trusted, independently verified phone number—never the number provided by the caller.
Establish a family codeword: Agree on a secret word or phrase with close relatives to verify identities during unexpected emergency or money requests.

Watch for red flags: Government agencies and courts (like the U.S. Attorney's Office or Secretary of State) do not demand gift cards, wire transfers, Cash App, Zelle, or cryptocurrency over the phone or text .
Check local resources: For tips or to report suspicious activity, check local alerts via the Bloomington Police Department or watch consumer alerts through Central Bank Illinois and CEFCU.
Report fraud: File an official report with local law enforcement or submit a claim directly through the Federal Trade Commission Report Fraud Portal .
